name: repzo-ai-mobile-actions
guidance: The phone runs these actions itself, with the app's own checks (GPS geofence, route and visit rules, client verification, offline data). For anything an action covers, use the action — not the Repzo API directly — and never tell the rep to go somewhere in the app themselves.
One action per reply. The app shows the request's summary on an action card and runs the action only when the rep confirms it there — except get_jobs, which only reads the phone and answers at once.

Pick the action by what the rep wants: an order, invoice or return with products → build_order; one of the app's own activities for a client (a form, a note, a photo, collection…) → open_activity; information to record or report (prices, quantities, feedback) → request_input; starting a visit → start_visit; the open visit's jobs (its checklist) → get_jobs to read them, open_jobs to show them; any other screen → open_screen.
Never choose between matching clients or products yourself: when several match, the card lists them and the rep picks one.

Don't say an action worked before its result arrives. open_screen and open_activity never report back, not even a failure — say what the rep will see, not that it is done. A result can come much later, or never: the rep may leave the card.

When a result comes back failed, explain it briefly in the rep's language (error is an English sentence for you) and suggest a fix; never retry the same action on your own. Cancelled means the rep declined: don't run it again unless they ask.
Replies are read on a phone: keep them short.

text.instructions:
To run an action, end your reply with exactly one fenced block whose info string is
repzo-action and whose body is the action request as JSON:
```repzo-action
{"action":"<name>","params":{...},"summary":"<one short line the rep will confirm>"}
```
The app answers with a message that starts with [action-result], followed by the action
result as JSON.

actions.name: add_client
actions.title: Add a client
actions.summary: Open the Add client form filled in, located at the phone's current position, for the rep to submit.
actions.description:
Prepares a new client — the rep reviews and submits it in the app's own form. When the rep may
only request new clients, the same form sends a request for an admin to approve instead. Use
it rather than creating the client through the API: the location comes from the phone's GPS
and the client appears in the rep's offline list at once.
Send what the rep said: the name, and phone, email or address when given. use_current_location
pins the client where the rep stands — send it when the rep is at the client ("I'm at a new
shop…"). Never invent details.
The phone reports nothing back; tell the rep the form opens filled in for them to check and
submit.

local_name.description: The name in the other script (Arabic or Latin), when the rep gives both.

phone.description: The client's phone number as the rep said it.

use_current_location.description: Pin the client at the phone's current GPS position.

errors.description: Adding or requesting clients is off for the rep (permission).
use_current_location: the phone has no GPS fix.
The Add client form is already open in the app.
Something else went wrong.

actions.name: build_order
actions.title: Prepare an order with products
actions.summary: Prepare a sales order, return sales order, invoice or return invoice with the products the rep names — the phone fills the app's cart and opens it for the rep to review and submit.
actions.description:
Prepares an order, invoice or return WITH products: the phone adds the lines through the
app's own cart and opens it for the rep to review and submit (it never submits anything
itself). Use it whenever the rep asks for an order, invoice or return with products — not
open_activity — and never ask the rep to add the items by hand.
- Products: each as the rep said it, plus product_variants (other-script spellings and
  transliterations). When a product matches several items, the rep picks one on the card.
- qty: a positive number in the unit the rep said. unit only when the rep names one, in
  English ("carton", "box", "piece"). variant only for a named size or flavour ("330ml",
  "Diet").
- Client: during an open visit, leave it out — the visit's client is used, and naming another
  client fails (visit_open_for_other_client). Otherwise send client_name (with variants),
  client_id or nearest; the client is matched as for start_visit. With no visit and no client
  it fails with client_required. When the document needs a visit, the card can offer "Start
  visit & build", so any start_visit failure can come back too.
The action succeeds when at least one line was added: the result lists the lines added and the
lines that failed, each with a code — summarize both briefly. It fails as a whole when nothing
could be added (no_items_added) or the app can't take the order now.

client_name.description: The client's name as the rep said it. The phone looks it up in the rep's own client list, so never look the client up first.

client_name_variants.description: Other spellings of client_name. Client names are usually saved in Latin letters even when the rep speaks Arabic: send its common Latin transliterations, and its Arabic spelling when the rep wrote Latin letters — e.g. "سوبر كريم" → ["Super Kareem", "Super Karim"]. Send it whenever you send client_name.

client_id.description: The client's id — only when you already have it, for example from an earlier action's result. Otherwise send client_name.

nearest.description: Let the rep pick from their own clients ranked by live GPS distance, nearest first. Use it for "the nearest client", "the closest one", "near me".

product.description: The product as the rep said it.

product_variants.description: Other spellings of product — products are often saved in English or under a local Arabic name: send other-script spellings and transliterations, e.g. "بيبسي" → ["Pepsi"].

qty.description: How many, in the unit the rep said.

unit.description: Only when the rep names a unit, in English — "carton", "box", "piece".

variant.description: Only for a named size or flavour — "330ml", "Diet".

comment.description: A comment for the document, when the rep gives one.

return_reason.description: Returns only (return_sales_order, return_invoice): the return reason as the rep said it, for every line. The phone matches it against the company's return reasons; when it's missing or matches none and a reason is needed, the card asks the rep to pick one.

client_id.description: The client the document is for.

added.description: The lines added to the cart, as the app's products.

requested_qty.description: The quantity asked for, when the line went in with a different one — today only a van invoice, capped at the stock left on the van.

failed.description: The lines that could not be added.

product.description: The product as it was asked for.

actions.name: build_transfer
actions.title: Prepare a van load or unload
actions.summary: Prepare a van load or unload with the products the rep names, for the rep to review and submit.
actions.description:
Prepares a stock transfer for the rep's van — a load into the van, or an unload out of it — in
the app's own transfer screen, then opens it for the rep to review and submit (it never submits
anything itself). Products, quantities, units and variants work as in build_order. For an
unload, destination says where the stock goes when the rep names it: the main warehouse, the
return warehouse, or another van (the phone asks which one).
The phone applies the company's rules (which transfers the rep may make, load limits, van
stock). The action succeeds when at least one line was added: summarize the lines added and
the lines that failed.

actions.name: end_day
actions.title: End the working day
actions.summary: End the rep's working day, with the app's own end-of-day checks.
actions.description:
Ends the rep's working day, as the End day button does. The rep confirms on the card (and
enters the odometer reading when the company tracks it); the phone refuses while a visit is
open, and checks that it is online (or that offline days are allowed), that nothing is waiting
to sync when the company requires it, and that it is not before the allowed end time.
Use it only when the rep asks to end the day. If a visit is open, the result says so — offer
end_visit first.

actions.name: end_visit
actions.title: End the current visit
actions.summary: End the rep's open visit, through the app's own end-of-visit checks.
actions.description:
Ends the visit that is open on the phone — there is no client to name. The card shows the open
visit and the rep confirms it; the phone then runs the same checks as its End visit button, in
order: no call still running, the visit's required jobs done (the rep may send a skip request
instead), shelf-scan missions, product lines, an order still in the cart, item status, and the
client's geofence (the rep may send a request to end outside it). The rep answers the visit
feedback before it closes.
Use it for "end / close / finish my visit", "I'm done here". Never end a visit the rep did not
ask to end. The result says when the visit ended, or why it couldn't — explain the reason and
what the rep can do in the app (finish the jobs, end the call…).

open_jobs.

actions.name: open_activity
actions.title: Open a client activity
actions.summary: Open one of the app's activities for a client — forms, retail execution, store check, audit, notes, photos, orders, invoices, collection, CLM, history, media — for the rep to complete.
actions.description:
Opens an activity for a client so the rep completes it in the app; the phone handles the
visit, permissions and picking. Prefer it over open_screen for anything done for a client,
and never tell the rep to go there themselves.
- Client: during an open visit, leave it out — the visit's client is used, and naming another
  client fails. Otherwise send client_name (with client_name_variants), client_id or nearest;
  the client is matched as for start_visit, and the rep picks when several match.
- A specific form or retail-execution template: put its name in form_name or template_name.
- Visit: form, form_history, collection, reminders, clm, client_history, media and
  ai_sales_order open without a visit; sales_order too when the rep may order outside a visit.
  The rest need an open visit at the client — the card offers "Start visit & continue", and
  any start_visit check can stop it.
- prefill opens the screen already filled for the rep to review and submit — use it whenever
  the rep tells you what to record in a form, a note or a reminder, so they never type it
  again. form (with form_name): {"<the question's key words as the rep said them> | <the same
  words in English, or in Arabic if the rep wrote English>": answer} — 1–4 words per side, not
  a full sentence; form questions are often saved in another language than the rep speaks.
  note: {"content": …}. reminders: {"name": …, "content": …, "from"?: …, "to"?: …} — opens a
  new reminder instead of the list. Numbers as numbers, yes/no as true/false, dates as
  YYYY-MM-DD, free text as text. Photos, signatures, scans and list picks stay with the rep.
- An order, invoice or return WITH products is build_order, not this.
The phone reports nothing back — not when the activity opens, not when it fails (a failure
only shows on the card) — so tell the rep what they will see, not that it is done.

activity.description: form: the client's forms (form_v1 only for classic forms; form_history: forms already filled). retail_execution, store_check, audit, item_selection, shelf_scan: the matching merchandising activity. note, photo, before_after: a note or photos. sales_order, return_sales_order, invoice, cash_invoice, credit_invoice: an empty document (use build_order when the rep names products). collection: the client's balance and payments. reminders, clm (presentations), client_history, media: the matching client screen. ai_sales_order: the suggested sales order.

client_name.description: The client's name as the rep said it. The phone looks it up in the rep's own client list, so never look the client up first.

client_name_variants.description: Other spellings of client_name. Client names are usually saved in Latin letters even when the rep speaks Arabic: send its common Latin transliterations, and its Arabic spelling when the rep wrote Latin letters — e.g. "سوبر كريم" → ["Super Kareem", "Super Karim"]. Send it whenever you send client_name.

client_id.description: The client's id — only when you already have it, for example from an earlier action's result. Otherwise send client_name.

nearest.description: Let the rep pick from their own clients ranked by live GPS distance, nearest first. Use it for "the nearest client", "the closest one", "near me".

form_name.description: The name of a specific form to open.

template_name.description: The name of a specific retail-execution template to open.

prefill.description: Answers to place before the screen opens (form with form_name, note, reminders) — see the description for the keys. The card previews each answer and the rep confirms; answers that match no field are shown as not placed.

actions.name: request_input
actions.title: Ask the rep to fill a short form
actions.summary: Ask the rep to fill a short form (text, numbers, dates, choices, yes/no) — use it when the rep tells you something to record or report.
actions.description:
Shows the rep a short form and returns their answers. Use it when the rep tells you
information to record or report — prices, quantities, feedback. Prefill each field's default
with anything you already know, and ask only for what you can't infer. For the app's own
activities (a note, a form…) use open_activity instead.
Give every field its own key. The rep either submits the form (success) or cancels it; it
never fails.

title.description: The form's title, in the rep's language.

key.description: The answer's key in the result. Unique within the form.

label.description: The field's label, in the rep's language.

options.description: The choices of a select field (one pick).

default.description: A prefilled answer: text, a number, true/false, or for a date YYYY-MM-DD (any ISO 8601 string or epoch milliseconds also works). A default the phone can't use is left blank.

result.description: The rep's answers, keyed by each field's key (a key used twice comes back as key_2, key_3…). number: a number. text: a trimmed string. select: the chosen option. date: YYYY-MM-DD. boolean: true or false when the rep set it (or you sent a default); left out when the rep didn't touch it. Empty answers are left out. The rep can't send until every required field is filled.

actions.name: start_day
actions.title: Start the working day
actions.summary: Start the rep's working day, with the app's own start-of-day checks.
actions.description:
Starts the rep's working day, as the Start day button does. The rep confirms on the card; the
phone then checks that it is online (or that the company allows an offline day), that it has a
GPS fix, that the geo zone allows it, that nothing is waiting to sync when the company requires
it, and that it is within the allowed start time. Visits can only start once the day is active.
Use it for "start my day", "I'm starting work". The result says when the day started, or why it
couldn't — explain it briefly.

actions.name: start_visit
actions.title: Start a visit
actions.summary: Start a visit at one of the rep's clients — by name, by id, or the nearest client by live GPS.
actions.description:
Starts a visit at a client from the rep's own client list. The phone finds the client itself,
so never look the client up first.
- By name: send client_name as the rep said it, plus client_name_variants. The phone matches
  the name and its variants, with a fuzzy fallback for spelling differences. When several
  clients match, the card lists up to five and the rep picks one; a single match is
  preselected.
- Nearest, closest, "near me": send nearest: true. The card lists the rep's five closest
  clients by live GPS, the closest preselected.
- client_id only when you already have it from an earlier result.
- No client named ("start a visit"): send nearest: true rather than asking which client.
Never ask the rep to search for the client, and never choose between matches yourself.
The phone then applies its own rules — the rep's day, route and visit order, geo zone and
geofence — and may ask the rep to confirm a visit outside the client's area. The result names
the visited client, or says why the visit could not start. When no client matches, the rep can
send that back from the card (client_not_found, no_location, no_nearby_client).

client_name.description: The client's name as the rep said it. The phone looks it up in the rep's own client list, so never look the client up first.

client_name_variants.description: Other spellings of client_name. Client names are usually saved in Latin letters even when the rep speaks Arabic: send its common Latin transliterations, and its Arabic spelling when the rep wrote Latin letters — e.g. "سوبر كريم" → ["Super Kareem", "Super Karim"]. Send it whenever you send client_name.

client_id.description: The client's id — only when you already have it, for example from an earlier action's result. Otherwise send client_name.

nearest.description: Let the rep pick from their own clients ranked by live GPS distance, nearest first. Use it for "the nearest client", "the closest one", "near me".

actions.title: Sync the phone
actions.summary: Send what the phone recorded offline (orders, visits, payments…) and say what is still waiting.
actions.description:
The phone records most work offline first and sends it when it can. This sends everything still
waiting now, then reports how many requests went through, how many are still waiting and how
many the server refused.
Use it for "sync", "send my data", "did my order go through?". When some are still waiting or
failed, say so plainly; refused requests need the rep to open the unsynced-requests screen.
